title: Uncountable pair colourings: positive results and counterexamples
summary: Sierpiński forbids uncountable homogeneous sets; Dushnik–Miller guarantees a large set in one colour or an infinite set in the other.
abstract: A set is homogeneous for a colouring of pairs if all its pairs receive the same colour. Ramsey’s theorem guarantees an infinite homogeneous set whenever pairs from an infinite set receive finitely many colours, but the corresponding uncountable assertion fails. There is a two-colouring of pairs from the first uncountable ordinal for which every uncountable subset uses both colours. A positive result survives when the target sizes differ: for every regular infinite cardinal, a two-colouring of pairs from a set of that size has either a homogeneous set of that cardinality in the first colour or a countably infinite homogeneous set in the second. The smaller target in the second colour makes this compatible with the counterexample.
